rationale: All three original findings resolved. CR-001: _detect_terminal_truncation now uses two independent guards matching _get_truncation_indicator exactly, short-circuit OR eliminated. CR-002: failed_result signature extended with finish_reason/truncated kwargs; invoke_task except branch forwards self._last_finish_reason/_last_truncated. CR-003: threading.Lock acquired non-blocking at top of invoke_task with try/finally release, enforcing single-concurrent-invocation invariant. No new issues introduced; backward compatibility preserved (new kwargs have defaults).

business_review.criterion: Truncation detection runs on terminal messages (final assistant answers), not only tool-call messages.
The state output API exposes a truncation signal (finish_reason / truncated), not just a bare output string.
The LiteLLM proxy path's max_tokens behavior is confirmed and covered by a regression test.
Regression tests cover the final-answer finish_reason=length / stop_reason=max_tokens case across providers (OpenAI/LiteLLM, native Claude, Bedrock).

standards_review.notes: Fix-up commit follows the required EPMCDME-14145: format.
threading.Lock is stdlib; new Optional[str] kwargs consistent with existing style.
No new files added in fix-up.

finding_status.notes: _detect_terminal_truncation now uses two independent if blocks (finish_reason then stop_reason), matching _get_truncation_indicator; short-circuit OR removed.
TaskResult.failed_result extended with finish_reason/truncated kwargs; invoke_task except branch forwards self._last_finish_reason/_last_truncated.
threading.Lock (_invoke_lock) added; invoke_task acquires non-blocking at entry, releases in finally; concurrent invocations now raise RuntimeError explicitly.
